result.summary:
Independently read docs/agents/design/REQ-032.md and docs/agents/design/REQ-032-schema.md in full (never substituted CODE-DESIGNER's/DATA-DESIGNER's result.summary), plus REQ-031.md/REQ-031-schema.md as the departure precedent, apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts (line 282), apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts's sendLedgeredNotification and NotificationKind union, apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts's notification_ledger table, and requirements.yaml's REQ-032 entry (all 7 ACs verbatim) directly from the file rather than from any handoff.

AC coverage (Sec6 map checked against every AC's ACTUAL text in requirements.yaml, not a paraphrase): all 7 ACs map to a concrete design element, no TBD/deferral language on any AC. AC1 -> Sec3.2 selection clauses (checked_in_at IS NULL / admission='admitted' / ends_at<=evaluationTime) + Sec3.4 step1 recheck + Sec4.1's five-button+other keyboard. AC2 -> Sec1.3 writeNoShowReason, the only write path. AC3 -> Sec3's single-job structural absence of a second/reminder job + Sec2's ledger-only reasoning (traced independently below). AC4 -> Sec0/Sec1 (isNoShow columnless, confirmed against actual schema.ts and 0001_tired_annihilus.sql -- no boolean no_show column exists anywhere). AC5 -> Sec1's rule table applied to the exact three constructed registrations (checked-in/admitted-not-checked-in/withdrawn), exactly one true. AC6 -> Sec3.3's classification:'transactional', verified against sendLedgeredNotification's actual code (domain/notification.ts lines ~116-120): a transactional send's code path never reads user.broadcastOptIn at all -- confirmed by reading the function body directly, not the design's claim about it. AC7 -> Sec5.1 explicitly instructs BACKEND-DEV's OWN Step 2 handoff result.issues to record the provisional-wording disclosure -- this is a process instruction TO BACKEND-DEV, not merely CODE-DESIGNER stating it did so itself, satisfying the specific check requested.

Props/types: fully specified with field-level detail throughout (isNoShow's 4-parameter signature and full first-match-wins rule table, NoShowReasonCode's closed 5-literal union, RegistrationNoShowContext/NoShowJobCandidate interfaces, writeNoShowReason/getRegistrationNoShowContext/selectRegistrationsForNoShowReasonRequest/makeNoShowReasonRequestJob signatures, formatNoShowTextPrompt/parseNoShowReplyContext with exact parse rules). No implementation code present -- every function is a signature plus a prose/table rule, never an executable body; consistent with the already-approved REQ-025/026/030/031 convention for this bot surface.

Tokens: Sec7 states explicitly and correctly that the bot surface has no visual/CSS component and references zero tokens from docs/Design system for AI agents/tokens/tokens.css -- verified true by inspecting the design for any color/spacing/typography reference: none exist. N/A check, not a silent skip.

SCHEMA-CHANGE CLAIM RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: grepped apps/bot/src myself for no_show_reason|noShowReason -- exactly one file matches, apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts itself (the column declaration at line 282 and its comment), confirming DATA-DESIGNER's claim that no handler/domain function/job/test currently reads or writes it. Column is nullable text, no CHECK, unchanged since REQ-011's 0001_tired_annihilus.sql. REQ-032-schema.md's decision to make zero migration is correct and sufficiently reasoned (Sec2.1-2.4: aggregation concern addressable via a plain CASE/GROUP BY over the existing column; no stated AC needs a split; splitting now would force CODE-DESIGNER's already-specified single write path to reshape, which is out of DATA-DESIGNER's mandate; the door stays open additively later). Also independently confirmed NotificationKind (domain/notification.ts) does NOT yet contain 'no_show_reason_request' -- correct, since the design proposes adding it, not claiming it already exists.

AC3 / RETRY-AFTER-FAILURE EDGE CASE -- TRACED EXPLICITLY AGAINST THE ACTUAL sendLedgeredNotification CODE (not the design's prose alone): the ledger INSERT (step 4 of domain/notification.ts) happens and commits BEFORE the actual Telegram send is ever attempted (step 5), and is never rolled back if step 5's send throws -- confirmed by reading the function body directly: a send failure returns {kind:'failed'} but the already-committed ledger row survives. Consequence for REQ-032's single-job design: (a) if the FIRST attempt's ledger insert succeeds and the actual send then fails, the row already exists in notification_ledger keyed (registrationId,'no_show_reason_request') -- a later T+24h/T+48h re-run's insert collides on that existing row (unique_violation) and returns skipped-already-sent, so NO second message is ever sent. This is under-sending (the person may never actually receive the ask), not over-asking -- and under-sending is explicitly the accepted, named risk this codebase's own REQ-025 Sec3.2/REQ-031 Sec5.2 already carry unmodified into every other ledgered job, not a new risk REQ-032 introduces. It does not violate AC3 (AC3 forbids a SECOND message, and under-sending produces at most one) and does not create an illegitimate second ask. (b) If the insert itself fails for a reason OTHER than uniqueness (e.g. a transient DB error), no row is committed at all, and a later re-run's insert is a genuine FIRST attempt, not a duplicate -- still at most one eventual send, just possibly delayed to T+24h/T+48h. In neither branch can the bare UNIQUE(registration_id,kind) constraint let a re-run re-prompt someone who was already durably marked as sent; the write-before-send ordering is precisely what makes this sound with no second job or asked-at column needed, matching Sec2's own reasoning (verified against the actual function, not merely asserted by the design doc, which phrases it slightly loosely as 'the first successful send inserts a ledger row' -- functionally the row is inserted regardless of subsequent send success, a wording imprecision worth a MINOR note but not a design defect since the mechanism it relies on is correct).

SINGLE-REF-LINE DISAMBIGUATION -- RE-DERIVED, NOT ASSERTED: constructed the analogous two-registrations-in-flight scenario Sec4.3 itself names (a person holding two admitted-not-checked-in registrations across different events, each with its own outstanding no-show ask). A reply to registration A's old force_reply prompt still carries 'No-show ref: <A's id>' verbatim -- parseNoShowReplyContext (Sec4.4) extracts A's id regardless of how many OTHER prompts are also outstanding, and Sec4.3 step6's ownership+existence check resolves against registration A specifically, then step7's gate checks ONLY A's own no_show_reason state. There is no cross-registration field-name collision to begin with, because (unlike REQ-031's liked/improve/topicVotes siblings competing for the SAME registration's reply-to-message routing) each registration here has exactly one free-text slot and its own independent ref line -- a reply to A's prompt can never be misrouted to B's column because Sec1.3's writeNoShowReason is always called with the registrationId PARSED FROM THAT SPECIFIC REPLY, never a freshly re-derived 'currently expected' registration id the way REQ-031's stale-reply bug depended on a freshly re-derived 'currently expected FIELD'. Confirmed: no REQ-031-analogous bug exists here; the departure from REQ-031's two-line ref+field mechanism to a one-line ref-only mechanism is reasoned soundly, not merely asserted.

DEPARTURES FROM REQ-031 CHECKED INDIVIDUALLY (task's explicit ask): (1) no reminder / single job -- sound, re-derived above via AC3 and the ledger's write-before-send ordering. (2) no asked-at column -- sound: unlike broadcast_opt_in's two-valued collision (true/false cannot encode 'never asked'), no_show_reason's NULL unambiguously means not-yet-answered and the once-only guarantee needed is 'was this SEND already attempted', which the ledger alone already answers; re-derived independently, not accepted on the design's own say-so. (3) single-field, no field-disambiguation line -- sound, re-derived above with a constructed scenario.

No stray files in project root. No YAML/JSON/Markdown format violation.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-032.md Sec2 (design question 2) phrases the ledger mechanism as 'the first successful send inserts a ledger row' -- imprecise, since sendLedgeredNotification actually inserts the ledger row BEFORE attempting the send and never rolls it back on a send failure (domain/notification.ts steps 4-5). The mechanism this phrasing describes is still correct in effect (a re-run cannot re-prompt once the row exists, regardless of whether the underlying send itself succeeded), so this does not block the gate, but BACKEND-DEV/future readers should not take the phrase 'first successful send' literally when reasoning about the under-sending risk this design inherits from REQ-025.
